To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth status of the children with congenital hypothyroidism detected by neonatal screening was impaired at the time of diagnosis, but it was improved during follow-up.
the head circumference of children with congenital hypothyroidism (CH) improved more rapidly compared to weight and height.
CH patients have impaired growth development which is improved during follow up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth status and growth pattern of children with CH in Isfahan province and the results of the current study could be used to evaluate the growth status of children with CH.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth pattern of CH infants was similar to that of regional controls in early childhood but it was significantly impaired in late childhood and adolescence.
the growth of CH patients was impaired in the first 3 years of life and it was improved in the next 2 years, and then the growth was normal in the 5th and 6th years.
the growth of CH patients is impaired and it is improved gradually during the follow up.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth status of children with CH is better than previously reported and they are not at risk for growth impairment.
CH patients have growth retardation which improves gradually and the growth charts of CH are different from regional healthy infants.
CH patients have a growth pattern different from normal children and the growth of these patients is improved by L-T4 replacement therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
growth status of CH patients can be monitored by the generated charts and the growth status of these patients can be compared with their healthy counterparts.
the growth charts generated in this study are useful tools for monitoring growth of patients with CH.
growth charts for CH patients should be generated in each region and used for the assessment of growth status of patients.
